title: Access Control Baseline
text: Enterprise systems enforce role based access control before retrieval. Finance roles can view invoices, HR roles can view benefits, legal roles can view contracts, and cross domain access requires governance approval plus immutable logging.

title: Privileged Access Review
text: Privileged administrator access is reviewed every thirty days. Dormant accounts older than forty five days are disabled. Emergency elevation expires after four hours and must include ticket id, business justification, and manager approval.

title: Audit Logging Requirements
text: Every RAG answer stores query id, retrieved document ids, chunk ids, model version, prompt template version, policy filters, latency, estimated cost, and user role. Audit records are immutable and retained for eighteen months.

title: PII Redaction Standard
text: Personally identifiable information is redacted before embeddings are written to a vector store. The service masks social security numbers, bank accounts, home addresses, patient identifiers, and payroll ids. Failures require severity one review and reindexing.

title: Data Classification Policy
text: Data is labeled public, internal, confidential, or restricted. Restricted data requires encryption, policy filtered retrieval, redacted embeddings, and quarterly access review. Public data may be indexed without approval after malware scanning.

title: Data Residency Rule
text: European employee records remain in the EU region. Customer billing data remains in the contracted cloud region. Cross region replication requires privacy approval, legal review, and a documented recovery objective.

title: Invoice Approval Workflow
text: Invoices above 50000 dollars require two approvals from the department owner and finance controller. Invoices below 50000 dollars require department owner approval. Emergency vendor payments must be reconciled by finance within three business days.

title: Expense Exception Handling
text: Travel expenses above policy limits need director approval and receipt evidence. Missing receipts are allowed only below 75 dollars. Repeated exceptions trigger finance review and manager notification.

title: Cost Center Chargeback
text: Monthly RAG spend is charged to business units by query volume, generation tokens, embedding tokens, reranking calls, storage, and vector index rebuilds. Shared platform cost is allocated by active application count.

title: Contract Retention Schedule
text: Executed customer contracts are retained for seven years after termination. Draft contracts are retained for two years. Litigation hold overrides the standard retention schedule and prevents deletion until legal releases the hold.

title: Ediscovery Hold Procedure
text: When litigation hold is active, deletion jobs pause for affected mailboxes, contracts, chat exports, and RAG audit logs. Legal must approve release before retention cleanup resumes.

title: Third Party Data Use Addendum
text: Vendors processing enterprise data must sign a data use addendum. The addendum limits training use, requires breach notification within forty eight hours, and permits annual security evidence review.

title: Benefits Enrollment Guide
text: Employees can change health benefits during open enrollment or after a qualifying life event. Qualifying events include marriage, birth, adoption, loss of coverage, and relocation. Documentation is due within thirty days.

title: Leave of Absence Policy
text: Medical leave requests require HR intake, manager notification, expected return date, and supporting documentation. Sensitive medical details are stored separately and excluded from general search indexing.

title: Employee Records Access
text: Managers can view job related employee records for direct reports. Compensation history and medical accommodation files are restricted to HR specialists and are not exposed to general RAG retrieval.

title: Vector Index Maintenance
text: The vector index is rebuilt weekly and incrementally updated every six hours. Each build records corpus snapshot hash, embedding model name, chunking parameters, index checksum, and promotion decision.

title: Model Cost Accounting
text: Embedding cost is calculated per input token and generation cost per output token. Reranking adds a per document scoring charge. Reports group RAG cost by business unit, retrieval strategy, top k, and generation model.

title: Cloud Operations Runbook
text: Cloud operations rotate service credentials every ninety days, verify backup completion daily, and fail over regional services only after health checks confirm sustained outage for ten minutes.

title: Incident Response Runbook
text: A production RAG incident begins with triage, blast radius assessment, retrieval log preservation, and customer impact analysis. The on call engineer freezes index updates when hallucinated answers are tied to stale chunks.

title: Stale Context Remediation
text: If retrieved context is stale, operators compare the answer timestamp with corpus snapshot time, quarantine outdated chunks, rebuild the affected index partition, and publish a correction notice for impacted users.

title: Service Level Objectives
text: The RAG API targets p95 latency below 1200 milliseconds for standard queries and below 2000 milliseconds for reranked compliance queries. Error rate must stay below one percent per rolling hour.

title: RAG Evaluation Policy
text: RAG releases require recall at k, mean reciprocal rank, normalized discounted cumulative gain, context precision, context recall, faithfulness, latency, and estimated cost. Increased hallucination risk blocks release without exception.

title: Human Review Sampling
text: High risk answers receive human review sampling. Compliance, medical, payroll, and legal answer categories require weekly review until two consecutive weeks meet faithfulness and context precision thresholds.

title: Benchmark Reproducibility Standard
text: Benchmark runs must record fixed seeds, dataset hash, configuration file, retriever variant, model profile, code commit, execution time, and artifact checksums for tables, traces, and figures.

title: Vendor Risk Intake
text: New AI vendors complete security questionnaire, data processing addendum, subprocessor disclosure, penetration test evidence, and financial risk assessment before production data access is approved.

title: Vendor Model Monitoring
text: Approved vendors are monitored for latency, availability, data retention changes, subprocessors, breach notices, and model deprecation. Critical vendor changes require architecture review before migration.

title: Procurement Approval Gates
text: Purchases above 100000 dollars require procurement review, security approval, legal approval, and finance controller sign off. Pilot tools below 10000 dollars still require data classification review.

title: Model Governance Policy
text: Model releases need documented owner, intended use, evaluation evidence, rollback plan, privacy assessment, and risk tier. High risk models require governance board approval before production deployment.

title: Prompt Template Change Control
text: Prompt templates are versioned. Material changes require offline evaluation, reviewer sign off, and prompt injection testing. Emergency prompt patches expire after seven days unless converted into a standard change.

title: Hallucination Exception Process
text: A hallucination exception must document user impact, root cause, compensating controls, expiration date, and owner. Exceptions cannot be renewed if faithfulness or context recall continues to regress.

title: Storage Encryption Standard
text: Object storage buckets use customer managed encryption keys for confidential and restricted data. Public buckets require explicit approval, logging, malware scanning, and quarterly access review.

title: Regional Failover Procedure
text: Regional failover starts with incident commander approval, dependency health checks, DNS traffic shift, database replica validation, and post failover cost review. Rollback requires stable primary health for thirty minutes.

title: Capacity Planning Guideline
text: Capacity planning uses peak query volume, embedding backlog, vector index size, reranker concurrency, generation token budget, and latency objective. Forecasts are refreshed monthly and before major product launches.

title: Risk Acceptance Register
text: Accepted risks record scope, business owner, residual risk rating, mitigation plan, review date, and expiration. Expired risks automatically return to open remediation status.

title: Policy Conflict Resolution
text: When policies conflict, restricted data handling takes precedence over cost optimization and convenience. Legal hold overrides retention deletion. Incident containment overrides routine indexing freshness.

title: Retrieval Filter Design
text: Retrieval filters apply tenant, role, data classification, region, and document status before similarity search. Filters are evaluated before reranking so unauthorized chunks never reach the model context.

title: Chunking Guidance
text: Enterprise documents are chunked by section boundaries when available. Long tables use row groups. Chunks store source document id, section title, effective date, classification, and checksum.

title: Answer Citation Requirements
text: Generated answers include citations to retrieved chunks for policy, finance, legal, and HR topics. Answers without supporting citations are marked unverified and excluded from automated workflows.
